title: What If Yellowstone's Supervolcano Erupted Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if Yellowstone erupted? Its biggest eruption was nearly 6,000 times bigger than Mount St. Helens.
Closest to the caldera, in Wyoming, Montana and Idaho, glowing pyroclastic flows would be the deadliest threat.
Ash would blanket the region and fall far downwind. Ash from an earlier eruption has been found in Iowa, Louisiana and California.
Ashfall would hit roads, power and crops across the middle of the country, getting thinner with distance.
Sulfur gases would cool the planet. After Pinatubo in 1991, global temperatures dropped for two to three years.
USGS says a caldera-forming eruption in the next few thousand years is exceedingly unlikely. Smaller hydrothermal blasts are the real risk.
